item.content:encoded:
Per the article:

As there is no known mechanism for halting SCP-871's replication, any uncontained instances could replicate exponentially, quickly becoming unmanageable. No maintainable plans for the containment of more than 20,000 instances of SCP-871 have yet been devised. It is estimated that an uncontrolled outbreak originating with a single instance would render the earth uninhabitable within 80 days.

Therefore, if you were to put SCP-871 in a room and lock it up, it would still continue to replicate. Since it requires somebody to consume the new replications every day, the maintenance needed to contain SCP-871 warrants it a Keter designation.

item.title: Cakes and Math
item.content:encoded:
To make the math more explicit for anyone running through the comments:

Given 237 cakes now, run the math backward, remembering that only uneaten cakes replicate, while eaten cakes are simply replaced:

237/2 = 118.5. 119 instances, 1 eaten.
119/2 = 59.5. 60 instances, 1 eaten.
60/2 = 30. 30 instances, none eaten.
30/2 = 15. 15 instances, none eaten.
15/2 = 7.5. 8 instances, 1 eaten.

Since 8 is 23, we now have a theoretical point at which the cake began to be consumed by D-Class, approximately three days after a presumed singular instance was contained.

item.content:encoded:
Nope. The event horizon corresponding to a stable black hole of the same mass would be increasing faster than light, but the actual physical event horizon cannot expand faster than light. Gravitational influences travel at the speed of light.

This assumes that cakes can replicate while being torn apart by relativistic oscillations and being thrown into quantum foam, or whatever weird stuff happens inside black holes. It also assumes that creation of mass ex nihilo doesn't change any other physical laws.

(Also, it's possible the event horizon wouldn't increase at all. The event horizon isn't a measure of what's inside the black hole so much as an effect of things falling inside. Whatever happens inside a black hole can't affect the outside.)

item.title: Re: 2 Questions regarding this
item.content:encoded:
To answer your first question, I would imagine that although no anomalous affects have been observed so far, Foundation personnel still aren't 100% sure that they won't manifest in the future. So they'll keep sending D-class in. Perhaps somewhere down the line they'll start letting their staff partake.

Regarding the termination, I'd imagine it's there so the staff know how far they're able to go in order to force the D-class to eat the cake - I doubt they're a regular occurrence. Once the D-class is told "eat the cake or we will kill you", I'm guessing most of them will eat the cake.

Regarding your second question;

Neither.

If you properly consume a Ketercake within 24 hours, one Ketercake will reappear in the same vicinity 24 hours later. You had one cake, you ate one cake, one cake reappears.

If you fail to eat the cake, or it's damaged, a second cake appears and the first one repairs itself. You had one cake, you didn't eat the cake - now you've got two cakes.

Both of these cakes will replicate themselves if they're not eaten.

The Foundation has 237 of these cakes.

The best thing the Foundation can do is keep the number of Ketercakes constant - they can't be reduced.

item.title: 2 Questions regarding this
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, is 'kill a D-Class' authorization really warranted here? I mean, I doubt it would ever be necessary since it's cake and who in their right, soon-to-be-executed-otherwise-anyway mind would refuse, let alone be able to resist if they're famished? And if that was the case, they could just another batch of D-Classes - or any Foundation member in the vicinity could eat it with the possible exception of Dr. Clef. It's not stated to be harmful besides cake poisoning, so I don't see why any researcher or doctor would turn down having cake at work (You're saving humanity, doing research, AND get the joy of eating cake!)

Secondly, going by the 237 cakes part, does that mean there's 237 instances of the cake and once they're eaten fully with no chance to replicate, there's no more SCP-871? Or is it the number of possible cake types that humanity has been exposed to, therefore a number that is liable to increase?
